method: Built-in image_gen.imagegen, transparent RGBA, using each existing card as visual reference. Sprite sheets are generated assets; no game rules were generated or altered.

prompts.fighter: Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: production 2D game character animation sprite sheet for an existing tactical arena. Derive the character identity from the supplied card reference, but return ONLY a new sprite sheet, not a card or UI mockup. A clean exact 4-column by 4-row grid on a truly transparent background, 16 equal square cells. One whole-body character in each cell. All 16 figures have the same size, same equipment, consistent painted game-render finish, camera about 35 degrees above the ground, restrained mature fantasy art, natural proportions, readable silhouette at 70 pixels, crisp detail without outlines. Feet are anchored at horizontal center and 88% of each cell height, body occupies about 72% of cell height, leave ample transparent space for weapon swings. No ground, no floor, no baked shadows, no grid lines, no text, no labels, no frame, no health bars, no UI. Animation layout: row 1 four consecutive WALK frames facing NORTH (back three-quarter view, walking away/up), alternating planted left foot / passing / planted right foot / passing. Row 2 the same WALK cycle facing SOUTH (front three-quarter view, approaching/down). Row 3 four ATTACK frames facing NORTH: anticipation, windup, strike/release, recovery. Row 4 four ATTACK frames facing SOUTH with the same sequence. Keep identity identical across all frames. Entire weapons and both feet always fit inside their own cell. Transparent RGBA output. Character: the Fighter from reference image 1: lean young adult male swordsman with tousled dark cobalt-blue hair, serious face, dark steel armor with restrained antique brass trim, a short royal-blue shoulder cape, steel sword held in his right hand. No bow, no shield, no helmet. Sword slashes visibly sweep through the attack frames. Athletic human silhouette, full-length armored legs and grounded boots. Use the reference only for character identity, exclude its gold card border and lettering.
